nodes.name: speech_energy
nodes.summary: How intensely the speaker is delivering. 0.8+ = emphatic/passionate. 0.3- = reflective/quiet.

details.detection: RMS amplitude normalized to speaker's range, smoothed over 500ms window. Future: Wav2Vec-BERT energy embedding (semantic energy, not just volume).
details.thresholds: 0.8+ = emphatic/passionate; 0.3- = reflective/quiet; mid-word edit point flag at 0.4-0.6 rising
details.rationale: Vocal intensity correlates with perceived importance (Scherer 2003 affect prosody)
details.qualityGate: If speech_energy at an edit point is mid-word (0.4-0.6 and rising), the cut landed badly

nodes.name: speech_energy_delta
nodes.summary: Whether the speaker is building up (positive) or winding down (negative).

details.detection: Derivative of speech_energy over 2s sliding window. Future: Wav2Vec-BERT temporal features capture energy trajectory natively.
details.thresholds: Rising delta = building (cut feels premature); falling delta = releasing
details.rationale: Pearlman's breath model — rising energy = inhale (building), falling = exhale (releasing)
details.qualityGate: A cut during rising delta (speaker building toward something) feels premature

nodes.name: speaking_rate_wpm
nodes.summary: How fast the speaker is talking relative to their own baseline.

details.detection: Word count / duration from Whisper timestamps, smoothed over 10s. Future: Grok provides more accurate word-level timestamps.
details.thresholds: > 180 WPM → readability issue (captions can't keep up)
details.rationale: Rate acceleration signals excitement or urgency; deceleration signals emphasis or gravity
details.qualityGate: If captions can't keep up with speaking_rate (> 180 WPM), flag readability issue

nodes.name: pitch_contour
nodes.summary: Intonation pattern. Rising = question/uncertainty. Falling = statement/finality. Rising-falling = emphasis.

details.detection: F0 extraction from audio, classified over phrase boundaries. Future: Wav2Vec-BERT captures pitch embedding directly.
details.output: enum — rising | falling | flat | rising-falling | falling-rising
details.rationale: Universal intonation patterns across languages (Bolinger 1978, Gussenhoven 2004)
details.qualityGate: N/A (informational signal, not a quality metric)

nodes.name: silence_duration_ms
nodes.summary: How long since speech stopped. Context-dependent meaning ranging from natural breath pause to dramatic pause to dead air.

details.detection: Gap between word-level timestamps from Whisper. Future: Grok + Wav2Vec-BERT distinguish intentional pauses from dead air.
details.thresholds: < 300ms = natural breath pause (ignore); 300-800ms = clause boundary or emphasis pause; 800-2000ms = topic boundary or dramatic pause; > 2000ms = potential dead air (check narrative_pressure before removing)
details.rationale: Event segmentation theory — pauses > 800ms treated as topic boundaries (engineering default, not from Zacks 2007 — Zacks researches event segmentation at seconds-to-minutes scale)
details.qualityGate: silence > silence_tolerance AND narrative_pressure < 0.5 → flag as dead air

nodes.name: emphasis_word
nodes.summary: Which specific words the speaker is stressing. These are natural zoom/graphic anchor points.

details.detection: Volume spike > 1.5x local average + duration stretch > 110% on specific word. Future: Wav2Vec-BERT stress detection identifies emphasized words semantically.
details.thresholds: Volume spike > 1.5x local average; duration stretch > 110%
details.rationale: Prosodic prominence correlates with information focus (Ladd 2008 intonational phonology)
implementsIn: Computed from Whisper word timestamps + audio amplitude analysis
details.qualityGate: If a zoom or graphic lands on a non-emphasized word, the system is off-target

nodes.name: filler_detected
nodes.summary: Non-content speech (um, uh, like, you_know, so, basically). Removal candidates in raw footage; should be gone in polished content.

details.detection: Whisper transcript + regex pattern matching + confidence threshold. Future: Wav2Vec-BERT classifies fillers with higher accuracy than text matching.
details.output: boolean per instance + type (um | uh | like | you_know | so | basically)
details.thresholds: filler_count > 0 in final output AND formality > 0.5 → flag
details.rationale: Fillers reduce perceived speaker competence (Brennan & Williams 1995)
details.qualityGate: filler_count > 0 in final output AND formality > 0.5 → flag

nodes.name: emotional_valence
nodes.summary: The emotional charge of what's being said/how it's being said. Voice-level detection catches mismatches between text and tone.

details.detection: Sentiment analysis on transcript text (limited — misses vocal tone). Future: Wav2Vec-BERT reads emotional valence from VOICE, not just words. 'I'm fine' in text = positive. 'I'm fine' said through tears = negative.
details.rationale: Vocal affect is cross-culturally recognized (Scherer 2003, Sauter et al. 2010)
implementsIn: Currently transcript-only. Future: Wav2Vec-BERT emotion classifier on fal.ai
details.qualityGate: If music_energy is high-positive AND emotional_valence is negative → mood mismatch

nodes.name: speaker_change
nodes.summary: A different person is now speaking. Enables interview editing, multi-speaker content.

details.detection: Not available (no diarization). Approximated from long pauses + content shift. Future: Grok speaker diarization — precise speaker boundaries with speaker labels.
details.rationale: Speaker changes are natural event boundaries (event segmentation theory)
implementsIn: Future: Grok on fal.ai. Current: heuristic from transcript gaps
details.qualityGate: If speaker_change detected but no visual change (still showing previous speaker) → flag

nodes.name: speech_formality
nodes.summary: How formal the speech is. Affects caption style, graphic style, overall tone matching.

details.detection: Vocabulary analysis + sentence structure + filler rate from transcript. Future: Combined transcript + Wav2Vec-BERT vocal register analysis.
details.rationale: Register mismatch between audio and visual treatment creates cognitive dissonance
implementsIn: Classifier on transcript features (avg sentence length, vocabulary tier, filler rate)
details.qualityGate: If speech_formality = casual AND formality genre_parameter > 0.7 → flag style mismatch

nodes.name: entity_number
nodes.summary: Speaker made a quantitative claim (count, percentage, currency, duration, comparison). Natural stat-graphic anchor points.

details.detection: NER + regex for numeric patterns in transcript. Future: Same (text-based signal, doesn't benefit from V-JEPA).
details.output: boolean per instance + value + type (count | percentage | currency | duration | comparison)
details.thresholds: If entity_number detected but no visual reinforcement AND moment_weight > 0.5 → missed opportunity
details.rationale: Dual-coding theory (Paivio 1971) — visual + auditory encoding of same data → 2x retention
details.qualityGate: If entity_number detected but no visual reinforcement AND moment_weight > 0.5 → missed opportunity

nodes.name: entity_CTA
nodes.summary: The speaker is asking the viewer to DO something. Almost always a high-weight moment.

details.detection: Imperative verb + action noun in final 25% of transcript. Future: Same (text-based).
details.output: boolean per instance + CTA_type (visit | subscribe | buy | download | contact | learn_more)
details.thresholds: Final 25% of transcript
details.rationale: CTA placement in final quarter correlates with higher conversion (Wistia data shows 16% avg CTA conversion rate; specific multiplier varies by content type)
details.qualityGate: If entity_CTA detected but no visual treatment (no lower-third, no zoom) → missed CTA

nodes.name: rhetorical_question
nodes.summary: Speaker asks a question they'll answer themselves. Creates an open loop — viewer's brain NEEDS the answer (Zeigarnik Effect).

details.detection: Question mark in transcript + no answer within 3s + speech_energy rising. Future: Wav2Vec-BERT can distinguish genuine questions (rising terminal pitch) from rhetorical.
details.thresholds: No answer within 3s
details.rationale: Zeigarnik Effect — unresolved questions create cognitive tension that drives retention
details.qualityGate: N/A (informational signal for technique triggering)

nodes.name: topic_boundary
nodes.summary: The speaker shifted topics. Event segmentation theory says the brain WANTS a perceptual reset at these boundaries.

details.detection: Cosine similarity between embedding of sentence N and sentence N+1. If delta > 0.3 (threshold), flag as topic boundary. Future: Same approach but with better embeddings from context-aware models.
details.output: boolean at each sentence boundary + confidence 0-1
details.thresholds: Cosine similarity delta > 0.3 between consecutive sentences
details.rationale: Event segmentation theory (Zacks & Swallow 2007) — semantic shifts = natural edit points
implementsIn: Gemini embedding on transcript sentences, cosine delta computation
details.qualityGate: If topic_boundary detected but no visual change within ±1s → flat edit

nodes.name: claim_strength
nodes.summary: How confidently the speaker states something. Assertive claims deserve emphasis. Hedged claims should not get stat graphics.

details.detection: Linguistic analysis — modal verbs ('might,' 'could' = hedged), superlatives ('best,' 'fastest' = assertive), citations ('studies show' = factual). Future: Same (text-based).
details.rationale: Perceived credibility correlates with visual emphasis alignment (Petty & Cacioppo ELM)
details.qualityGate: If claim_strength = hedged AND stat_graphic applied → visual overpromise

nodes.name: narrative_phase
nodes.summary: Where we are in the story arc. Every narrative — even a 30s ad — has phases.

details.detection: Composite of position_in_video + speech_energy curve + topic_boundary count. First 15% = opening. energy rising = build. energy peak = climax. energy falling = resolve. Final 15% = closing/CTA. Future: LLM reads transcript and assigns phases semantically (more accurate for non-linear structures).
details.output: enum — opening | setup | build | climax | resolve | cta | closing
details.thresholds: First 15% = opening; final 15% = closing/CTA
details.rationale: Vonnegut's story shapes — every narrative is a curve on a good-fortune axis
implementsIn: Computed from speech_energy time series + position + entity_CTA detection
details.qualityGate: If narrative_phase = climax AND edit_density is LOWER than build phase → anticlimax

nodes.name: motion_intensity
nodes.summary: How much visual change is happening. 0.8+ = fast action/camera movement. 0.2- = static/talking head.

details.detection: Optical flow magnitude averaged across frame, normalized. Future: V-JEPA 2 motion features — understands not just 'something moved' but 'what kind of movement'.
details.thresholds: 0.8+ = fast action; 0.2- = static
details.rationale: Visual motion is the strongest driver of attentional capture (Abrams & Christ 2003)
details.qualityGate: motion_intensity spike at a cut point = cut-on-action (good). Spike 3 frames before cut = premature

nodes.name: motion_type
nodes.summary: Whether the subject or the camera (or both) is creating the motion.

details.detection: Heuristic from optical flow distribution (uniform = camera, localized = subject). Future: V-JEPA 2 distinguishes subject action from camera motion natively.
details.rationale: Blain Brown's motivated camera — camera movement must have a WHY. Subject movement is inherent
details.qualityGate: camera_moving without motivated cause = unmotivated movement (flag if formality > 0.6)

nodes.name: action_type
nodes.summary: What the subject is physically doing. Determines appropriate shot duration, cut timing, and SFX.

details.detection: Gemini Vision keyframe description (text-based, imprecise). Future: V-JEPA 2 action recognition — 'person picks up cup' not 'person near cup.' 39.7 recall@5 on Epic-Kitchens action anticipation.
details.output: enum — talking | walking | gesturing | demonstrating | eating | writing | still | interacting_with_object | other
details.rationale: Action boundaries are the strongest natural cut points (event segmentation theory)
implementsIn: Currently Gemini Vision. Future: V-JEPA 2 on fal.ai
details.qualityGate: If action_type = demonstrating AND shot_scale = EWS → subject too small to see demo

nodes.name: shot_scale
nodes.summary: How close we are to the subject. Determines emotional intimacy of the shot.

details.detection: Face detection bounding box size relative to frame. Face > 60% of frame height = ECU. 40-60% = CU. 25-40% = MCU. 15-25% = MS. < 15% = WS. No face detected = WS or EWS (use scene complexity to distinguish). Future: V-JEPA 2 + face detection provides more nuanced scale classification.
details.output: enum — ECU | CU | MCU | MS | MWS | WS | EWS
details.thresholds: Face > 60% frame height = ECU; 40-60% = CU; 25-40% = MCU; 15-25% = MS; < 15% = WS
details.rationale: Close-up frequency correlates with mental state attribution (Bálint et al. 2020)
details.qualityGate: 3+ consecutive shots at same scale → visual monotony flag

nodes.name: shot_composition
nodes.summary: Where the subject is placed in the frame. Affects transition planning (eye-trace continuity).

details.detection: Subject position relative to frame grid (face centroid or largest region centroid). Future: V-JEPA 2 subject localization provides more reliable centroid.
details.output: enum — center | rule_of_thirds | off_center | symmetric | dutch
details.rationale: Gestalt principle of figure-ground — composition determines what reads as 'subject' vs 'background'
implementsIn: Computed from face detection or saliency map
details.qualityGate: Subject at frame-right in shot A → subject at frame-left in shot B = good eye-trace flow (Murch #4)

nodes.name: face_present
nodes.summary: Whether a face is visible, where it is, how large. Faces are the strongest attention magnets.

details.detection: Face detection model (MTCNN or similar). Future: V-JEPA 2 multi-person tracking with persistent identity.
details.output: boolean + position (x,y normalized 0-1) + size (fraction of frame) + count
details.thresholds: Unsafe zone: top 10% or bottom 20%
details.rationale: Faces activate fusiform face area — fastest attentional capture in human vision (Hershler & Hochstein 2005)
details.qualityGate: If face_present AND face is in unsafe zone (top 10% or bottom 20%) → composition issue

nodes.name: face_emotion
nodes.summary: What the face is expressing. Informs color treatment, music mood, and cut timing.

details.detection: Facial expression classifier on detected face. Future: V-JEPA 2 reads emotional dynamics (transition from neutral to happy), not just static expression.
details.output: enum — happy | sad | angry | surprised | fearful | disgusted | neutral | contempt
details.rationale: Facial expressions are cross-culturally recognized (Ekman 1992, with cultural modifiers)
implementsIn: Emotion classification model on face crop
details.qualityGate: If face_emotion = sad AND music_energy = high-positive → mood mismatch

nodes.name: eye_contact
nodes.summary: Whether the subject is looking at the camera (= at the viewer). Direct address vs observation.

details.detection: Gaze direction estimation from face landmarks. Future: V-JEPA 2 provides temporal gaze tracking (when eye contact begins/ends).
details.output: boolean (looking at camera vs. looking away) + confidence 0-1
details.rationale: Direct gaze activates social cognition networks (Senju & Johnson 2009). Feels like being 'spoken to'
implementsIn: Gaze estimation from face detection pipeline
details.qualityGate: If eye_contact = true AND shot_composition = off_center → the subject is looking at nothing (recompose)

nodes.name: color_temperature
nodes.summary: The warmth or coolness of the visual. Affects mood, grade decisions, transition compatibility.

details.detection: Average color temperature from frame histogram analysis. Future: Per-region color analysis for more nuanced temperature mapping.
details.output: integer Kelvin estimate (2700-9000K) + enum (warm | neutral | cool)
details.thresholds: Color temperature delta > 1500K between consecutive scenes AND dissolve → ugly blend
details.rationale: Color-emotion associations (warm = comfort/nostalgia, cool = professional/melancholy) — Valdez & Mehrabian 1994
implementsIn: Frame color analysis in five-track pipeline
details.qualityGate: color_temperature delta > 1500K between consecutive scenes AND dissolve transition → ugly blend

nodes.name: visual_complexity
nodes.summary: How much visual information is in the frame. Fast cuts on complex frames = cognitive overload. Slow cuts on simple frames = boredom.

details.detection: Edge density + color histogram entropy, normalized. Future: V-JEPA 2 scene understanding provides semantic complexity (not just edge count).
details.thresholds: visual_complexity > 0.7 AND time_since_last_cut < 1.5s → information overload
details.rationale: Cognitive load theory — working memory can hold 4±1 items (Cowan 2001, not Sweller 1988). Complex frames use more slots
implementsIn: Computed from edge detection + histogram analysis
details.qualityGate: If visual_complexity > 0.7 AND time_since_last_cut < 1.5s → information overload flag

nodes.name: screen_direction
nodes.summary: Which direction the subject faces or moves. Critical for continuity editing.

details.detection: Face orientation from face detection + subject position in frame. Future: V-JEPA 2 subject tracking with directional understanding.
details.rationale: 180-degree rule — screen direction must be consistent across cuts or viewer loses spatial orientation
details.qualityGate: screen_direction flips between cuts without motivated camera movement → continuity break

nodes.name: scene_type
nodes.summary: The environment. Affects ambient sound design, color treatment expectations, shot duration norms.

details.detection: Scene classification from Gemini Vision. Future: V-JEPA 2 scene understanding with environmental semantics.
details.output: enum — indoor | outdoor | studio | abstract | graphic_only | screencast | mixed
details.rationale: Environmental context sets viewer expectations (indoor = intimate, outdoor = expansive)
details.qualityGate: If scene_type changes but ambient_bed doesn't → audio-visual environment mismatch

nodes.name: ai_artifact_risk
nodes.summary: How likely the current frame window contains AI generation artifacts. Used to trigger preventive cuts before artifacts appear.

details.detection: Frame-to-frame diff analysis. High temporal inconsistency (flicker, morphing) scores high. Specific checks: face consistency (landmark drift), hand integrity (topology check), background stability. Future: V-JEPA 2 temporal consistency features — predicts what SHOULD happen next, high prediction error on actual frames = artifact.
details.thresholds: ai_artifact_risk > 0.6 AND shot held > 3s → immediate cut. Temporal consistency degrades after ~3-4s in current models
details.rationale: AI-specific signal. No traditional film theory equivalent. Temporal consistency degrades after ~3-4s in current models
implementsIn: Frame diff analysis + specific artifact detectors (face landmark drift, edge stability)
details.qualityGate: If ai_artifact_risk > 0.6 AND shot has been held > 3s → immediate cut recommended

nodes.name: music_energy
nodes.summary: Overall intensity of the music. Determines visual energy matching.

details.detection: Spectral analysis — weighted RMS across frequency bands. Future: Same approach, potentially enhanced with music understanding models.
details.rationale: Cross-modal correspondence — auditory intensity maps to visual intensity (Spence 2011)
details.qualityGate: If music_energy and visual edit_density move in opposite directions → energy mismatch

nodes.name: music_beat
nodes.summary: Where the musical beats fall. Natural edit sync points — cuts feel 'right' on beats.

details.detection: Spectral flux onset detection, classified by metric position. Future: Same, potentially with music structure model for more accurate downbeat detection.
details.output: array of timestamps (ms) + beat_type (downbeat | upbeat | offbeat)
details.thresholds: 4+ consecutive cuts on exact beat positions → metronomic flag
details.rationale: Neural entrainment — the brain synchronizes to rhythmic stimuli (Large & Palmer 2002)
details.qualityGate: If cuts are beat-synced AND all on exact beat positions for 4+ consecutive cuts → metronomic flag

nodes.name: music_section
nodes.summary: Where we are in the song structure. Sections map to edit density and transition types.

details.detection: Energy curve + repetition analysis + spectral change points. Future: Music structure analysis model (more accurate section boundaries).
details.output: enum — intro | verse | pre_chorus | chorus | drop | bridge | breakdown | outro | transition
details.thresholds: intro = sparse edits; chorus/drop = peak edit density; breakdown = pull back; outro = resolve
details.rationale: Musical form creates expectation patterns — chorus = energy peak is culturally universal in pop music
details.qualityGate: If music_section = chorus AND edit_density < build_section density → anticlimax

nodes.name: music_key
nodes.summary: Musical key and mode. Major = happy/triumphant. Minor = sad/dramatic. Lydian = dreamy.

details.detection: Chroma analysis → key estimation. Future: Same approach.
details.output: note (C-B) + mode (major | minor | dorian | mixolydian | lydian | pentatonic_major | pentatonic_minor)
details.rationale: Mode-emotion associations are culturally robust in Western music (Hevner 1935, updated)
details.qualityGate: N/A (informational for creative decisions, not quality metric)

nodes.name: music_bpm
nodes.summary: Tempo. Directly determines edit rhythm when beat-syncing.

details.detection: Autocorrelation on onset detection function. Future: Same approach.
details.thresholds: 40-60 = meditative; 80-100 = moderate; 120-140 = energetic; 160+ = intense; BPM > 140 AND pacing_tolerance > 5s → mismatch
details.rationale: Tempo-arousal correlation is one of the strongest in music psychology (Husain et al. 2002)
details.qualityGate: If BPM > 140 AND pacing_tolerance > 5s → music wants fast cuts, genre wants slow — mismatch

nodes.name: ambient_type
nodes.summary: Background environmental sound. Critical for continuity — ambient should not abruptly change at cuts.

details.detection: Audio classification on non-speech segments. Future: Wav2Vec-BERT environmental audio classification.
details.output: enum — room_tone | outdoor_wind | outdoor_city | crowd | nature | mechanical | silent | music_only
details.rationale: Chion's ambient bed theory — 'true silence = technical error.' Environment is always present
details.qualityGate: If ambient_type changes at a hard cut without fade → ambient discontinuity

nodes.name: position_in_video
nodes.summary: Where we are in the overall timeline. Affects moment_weight expectations.

details.detection: frame_number / total_frames
details.thresholds: 0.0-0.1 = hook zone (high energy, grab attention); 0.8-1.0 = CTA/closing zone
details.rationale: Hook zone in opening 10% drives retention; closing zone is CTA territory
details.qualityGate: If position 0.0-0.05 AND no strong visual hook → retention risk

nodes.name: time_since_last_cut
nodes.summary: How long the current shot has been held. Compared against pacing_tolerance.

details.detection: Current frame timestamp - last edit point timestamp
details.thresholds: time_since_last_cut > pacing_tolerance × 1.5 → 'overheld' flag
details.rationale: Shots held too long create boredom; under pacing_tolerance creates anxiety
details.qualityGate: time_since_last_cut > pacing_tolerance × 1.5 → 'overheld' flag

nodes.name: time_since_last_zoom
nodes.summary: Prevents zoom clustering. Two zooms too close feels amateur.

details.detection: Current frame timestamp - last zoom decision timestamp
details.thresholds: time_since_last_zoom < 2.0s → zoom too soon flag
details.rationale: Two zooms in close proximity feels amateur
details.qualityGate: time_since_last_zoom < 2.0s → zoom too soon flag

nodes.name: time_since_last_graphic
nodes.summary: Prevents graphic overload. Graphics need breathing room.

details.detection: Current frame timestamp - last graphic overlay timestamp
details.thresholds: time_since_last_graphic < 3.0s AND graphic_density > genre target → clutter flag
details.rationale: Graphics need breathing room to be readable and not feel overloaded
details.qualityGate: time_since_last_graphic < 3.0s AND graphic_density > genre target → clutter flag

nodes.name: active_overlays_count
nodes.summary: Visual clutter level. More than 2 simultaneous overlays (excluding captions) is usually too many.

details.detection: Count of currently visible overlays on timeline
details.thresholds: active_overlays_count > 3 → visual overload flag
details.rationale: Too many overlays compete for attention and create cognitive overload
implementsIn: Computed from overlay state at current frame
details.qualityGate: active_overlays_count > 3 → visual overload flag

nodes.name: cumulative_edit_density
nodes.summary: Overall edit intensity. Compared against transition_density genre parameter.

details.detection: Total edit decisions / video duration so far
details.thresholds: cumulative_edit_density diverges > 30% from genre target → density mismatch
details.rationale: Edit intensity should match genre expectations
details.qualityGate: If cumulative_edit_density diverges > 30% from genre target → density mismatch

nodes.name: scene_index
nodes.summary: Which scene we're in. Useful for scene-level decisions (first scene = establish, last scene = resolve).

details.detection: From scene parser output
details.rationale: Scene position drives establishment vs resolution treatment
details.qualityGate: N/A (structural reference)

nodes.name: narrative_pressure
nodes.summary: Is this a 'charged' silence? When narrative_pressure is HIGH, the system should NOT cut — the silence IS the content.

details.detection: Weighted combination of: position_in_video > 0.8 (contributes 0.3 if true) + silence_after_question (contributes 0.2 if true) + silence_after_strong_claim (contributes 0.2 if true) + speech_energy_delta sharply negative (contributes 0.3 × |delta|) + claim_strength = assertive in previous sentence (contributes 0.1). Future: V-JEPA prediction gap (expected motion - actual motion) feeds directly into this. JEPA World Model predicts emotional impact of holding vs cutting.
details.thresholds: narrative_pressure > 0.6 AND system removed the silence → quality degradation
details.rationale: Tarkovsky's time-pressure — a shot's pressure comes from accumulated narrative context, not from visual activity. The Nolan spinning top, scaled for commercial content.
implementsIn: Computed from other signals, new composite function
details.qualityGate: If narrative_pressure > 0.6 AND system removed the silence → quality degradation

nodes.name: reaction_moment
nodes.summary: The moment where cutting to the LISTENER's reaction is more powerful than staying on the speaker. Fincher's deposition, K-drama reaction holds.

details.detection: Current: Limited. speech_ends + face_present + pause > 500ms (approximation). Future: Grok speaker boundary (person A stops speaking) + V-JEPA face detection on non-speaker (person B visible) + face_emotion shift on person B (neutral → surprised, or neutral → moved). Intensity = magnitude of emotion shift on listener's face.
details.thresholds: pause > 500ms required; LOW CONFIDENCE until Phase 2 — should only suggest, never auto-apply
details.rationale: Mirror neuron response — viewers empathize with faces they see reacting, not speaking (Gallese & Guerra 2012)
implementsIn: Future: composite of Grok + V-JEPA multi-person tracking
details.qualityGate: If reaction_moment fires but no cut-to-listener within 1s → missed reaction opportunity

nodes.name: montage_mode
nodes.summary: The content has entered a montage section — music-driven, visually rhythmic, no continuous speech. Edgar Wright territory: the cuts ARE the content.

details.detection: All of the following simultaneously: music_section = chorus | drop + consecutive shots < 2s for 3+ shots + speech_energy < 0.3 (music is dominant, not speech) + music_energy > 0.6
details.thresholds: music_section in {chorus, drop}; consecutive shots < 2s for 3+ shots; speech_energy < 0.3; music_energy > 0.6
details.rationale: Eisenstein's metric montage — cuts at fixed intervals create mechanical tension and energy
implementsIn: Composite of music analysis + shot duration tracking + speech analysis
details.qualityGate: If montage_mode AND transition types are varied (3+ different types in 10s) → indecisive flag

nodes.name: cinematic_moment
nodes.summary: A moment where multiple dimensions align — speaker hits key point while music builds and camera pushes in. Natural climax points.

details.detection: Multi-track peak correlation from 5-Track analysis. 2+ tracks peak within 500ms = cinematic moment. Tracks: speech energy, motion, audio energy, beat. Future: V-JEPA temporal features + Wav2Vec-BERT emphasis detection for more accurate correlation.
details.thresholds: 2+ tracks peak within 500ms = cinematic moment
details.rationale: Cross-modal reinforcement — aligned multi-sensory peaks create stronger emotional response
details.qualityGate: If cinematic_moment detected AND no editing emphasis applied → wasted peak

nodes.name: eye_trace_position
nodes.summary: Where the viewer is LOOKING right now. Murch's Rule #4 (eye-trace, 7% weight). Cuts that force gaze jumps > 30% of frame width are perceptible and disruptive.

details.detection: Composite heuristic: 1. If face_present: eye_trace is at the face (faces are the strongest gaze attractor). 2. Else if motion detected: eye_trace follows the motion (gaze tracks moving objects). 3. Else: eye_trace is at the highest-contrast or brightest region of the frame. 4. If text on screen: eye_trace is at the text (reading overrides all other attractors). Weight: face > text > motion > contrast > brightness > center bias. Future: V-JEPA saliency maps provide per-frame attention prediction directly.
details.output: (x, y) normalized 0-1 coordinates — estimated position of viewer's gaze focus
details.thresholds: Distance between outgoing last frame and incoming first frame > 0.3 (normalized frame diagonal) → eye-trace discontinuity. Gaze jump > 30% of frame width is perceptible.
details.rationale: Tim Smith's DIEM project — professional editors achieve 80%+ gaze convergence (nearly everyone looks at the same spot). Viewers make ~20 fixations per average shot, attending to < 4% of screen area.
implementsIn: Composite computation from face detection, optical flow, saliency map
details.qualityGate: At each cut: if distance between eye_trace_position of outgoing last frame and incoming first frame > 0.3 (normalized frame diagonal) → eye-trace discontinuity flag

nodes.name: movement_phrase_phase
nodes.summary: Where we are in a physical movement phrase — like a musical phrase but for visual motion. Pearlman's kinesthetic rhythm.

details.detection: Computed from motion_intensity trajectory over 3-5s window: motion_intensity rising steadily → building; motion_intensity at local maximum → peak; motion_intensity falling after peak → releasing; motion_intensity stable and low (< 0.2) → rest. Future: V-JEPA temporal features capture movement phrase structure natively.
details.thresholds: motion_intensity stable and low (< 0.2) → rest
details.rationale: Karen Pearlman's Cutting Rhythms — editing has phrase structure like music and dance. Viewers physically empathize with on-screen movement (kinesthetic empathy / mirror neurons). Cutting at the wrong phase of a movement phrase creates physical discomfort in the viewer. Cutting at peak = cut-on-action (invisible). Cutting during build = premature. Cutting during release = comfortable resolution. Cutting during rest = neutral.
implementsIn: Computed from motion_intensity time series trajectory analysis
details.qualityGate: Cuts during 'building' phase (motion rising but hasn't peaked) → flag as premature cut

edges.label: Derivative of speech_energy over 2s sliding window
First 15% = opening; Final 15% = closing/CTA
